articles.title: NASCAR star sends chilling warning as series drops hammer on 'cowards' who attacked driver

paras.en: NASCAR has dropped the hammer on the crew that jumped, attacked, and beat two-time Cup Series winner Corey Heim in front of a Martinsville hot dog shack last weekend.

The series issued several major penalties and suspensions to both Chad Bryant and Steve Civatarese, suspending both indefinitely from NASCAR events — as well as the 2027 event at Martinsville. Both are also on probation for a year.

Bryant, the team owner at the center of last Saturday's confrontation, was fined $2,000 and must attend anger management through a NASCAR-approved program. Civatarese was fined $1,000. Five others were also fined and put on probation.
Denny Hamlin warns NASCAR over recent fights

- I believe this is one of the biggest, if not the biggest penalty handed down by NASCAR for a late model race. Remember, this wasn't an ARCA, Truck, O'Reilly or Cup race. This was a late model race. The sanctioning body rarely gets involved with those races.

- The fines are fairly tiny, if we're being honest. Five other crew members were also fined $500 each. Not sure NASCAR is really setting a precedent there. I could afford that, and I ain't exactly getting paid the big bucks over here.
- Chad Bryant having to attend anger management is probably fair given the video. I wonder if he reduces his suspension/probation time when he's done?
- Again, this is abnormal for NASCAR to get involved in a race at this level, which shows you A) how bad it was, but B) they listen to drivers/fans/social media more than any other sport.

Denny Hamlin, who is the unofficial spokesperson for the entire Cup garage, went on his "Actions Detrimental" podcast on Monday, absolutely ripped everyone involved, and then sent a fairly strong warning to NASCAR.

"Complete Classlessness. Yeah. From Chad Bryant, the owner and his team to wait on Corey ... Listen to what they did. Those cowards waited on Corey Heim to leave his car and leave his team and then jump him while he was on the way to his hauler," Hamlin said. "I don't know who's in charge of NASCAR regional, but there's absolutely no way that though any of those guys should be in a pit lane for the next year at least.
"I want them to say publicly what they do to them. And if it's nothing, I will have a major problem. But none of those cowards should be in a pit lane in the foreseeable future."
Hamlin went on to say that NASCAR had to "get control" of Martinsville, adding that it was "spiraling out of control."
Not sure these penalties and suspensions did quite that, but I suppose they do send a message. I reckon we'll see down the road if anyone received it.
"I got no respect for those guys," Hamlin added.

articles.title: Israeli minister claims ‘terrorist’ wanted to crash plane after Israel-bound flight’s emergency landing – latest
articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)

paras.en: The FlyDubai flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia this morning after transmitting emergency signals.
According to Israeli media, a fight had broken out between the plane’s two pilots. Passengers described one of the pilots being seriously injured in an alleged stabbing.

The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli officials said had between 160 and 180 passengers on board, transmitted a general emergency signal about two and a half hours after departing from Dubai, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.
It diverted to Saudi Arabia as it flew over Jordanian airspace, transmitting another emergency signal that indicated what is known as a possible unlawful interference.
The plane again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport.

The aircraft’s data appeared to show that it had suddenly and rapidly descended by nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the first emergency signal. It was not immediately clear who transmitted the emergency signals.
Tabuk airport said the plane landed at 9.45am local time and that both pilots were taken to hospital after sustaining injuries.
The Israeli prime minister’s office said the situation was “under control” and that steps were being taken to bring the passengers to Israel.

In a video from inside the plane that was reposted by Israeli social media users, one passenger, blood dripping from an open wound on his head, pleaded for assistance and said they were descending into Saudi Arabia, with which Israel has no diplomatic relations.
“We are here during an attack on the plane. We just subdued the terrorists and are preparing to land,” the man said in Hebrew.
“Anyone who can hear me, we need help. We are about to land in Tabuk, apparently in Saudi Arabia. An unknown area. All the passengers are safe and well, except for the pilot. We need help.”
A key piece of information from the FlyDubai flight is that someone in the cockpit transmitted emergency codes.
Pilots use four-digit ‘squawk codes’ to broadcast their position for air traffic control. These are used for routine flight but also in emergency situations.
Aircraft trackers at Flight Radar say the FlyDubai plane transmitted both emergency and hijack signals.
The plane transmitted a 7700 squawk code that means emergency. It also transmitted a 7500 squawk code, which can mean a hijacking.
These codes have to be manually entered from the cockpit.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the plane was “pretty much out of control” when the stabbing took place over Jordan on the flight’s path from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

“The co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane,” she told reporters by speakerphone held up by her mother who was waiting at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv.
“It was really on the way to crashing and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralised him,” she said.

“There was also a doctor who gave first aid and people who treated both of them. Other than the pilot, there were no injuries but the bigger fear was really a crash, which is exactly what he was trying to do.”
Her mother, Yasmin Abukasis, said her daughter was on the flight to attend a service for her brother killed in the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack.
Her daughter “thought they were going to die”, Abukasis told AFP, adding that one woman “went to the [cockpit] and saw a lot of blood”.
She said that two other pilots were on the plane and took charge, diverting it to Saudi Arabia.

A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel has been forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, after an apparent brawl between its pilots prompted distress signals that briefly raised fears of an attempted hijacking.
The flydubai flight was over Jordan when it diverted to Saudi Arabia, transmitting three emergency signals, one of which indicated a possible unlawful interference.
The plane dipped dramatically during the reported fight, descending about 16,000ft in just two minutes.
Israeli officials scrambled fighter jets, fearful of a possible hijacking attempt on a plane containing dozens of Israelis, and the plane landed at Tabuk airport in north-western Saudi Arabia.

A passenger told the Jerusalem Post that one pilot stabbed another and tried to force him out of the cockpit, prompting other Israelis to rush into the cockpit and subdue the attacker as the plane began to plunge.
It was not immediately possible to verify those reports. Pictures of a passenger with blood on their shirt were published by Israeli media.
A spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister’s office initially said that the flight diversion was not because of a hijack attempt; authorities later said they were investigating.
The FlyDubai flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia this morning after transmitting emergency signals.
According to Israeli media, a fight had broken out between the plane’s two pilots. Passengers described one of the pilots being seriously injured in an alleged stabbing.

The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli officials said had between 160 and 180 passengers on board, transmitted a general emergency signal about two and a half hours after departing from Dubai, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.
It diverted to Saudi Arabia as it flew over Jordanian airspace, transmitting another emergency signal that indicated what is known as a possible unlawful interference.
The plane again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport.

The aircraft’s data appeared to show that it had suddenly and rapidly descended by nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the first emergency signal. It was not immediately clear who transmitted the emergency signals.
Tabuk airport said the plane landed at 9.45am local time and that both pilots were taken to hospital after sustaining injuries.
The Israeli prime minister’s office said the situation was “under control” and that steps were being taken to bring the passengers to Israel.
Israeli minister claims 'terrorist' attempted to crash plane bound for Tel Aviv

An Israeli minister has decried what he described as a “terrorist” incident to kill Israelis after a flight was forced to land in Saudi Arabia when a physical altercation between the pilot and co-pilot prompted initial fears of a hijacking.

A Boeing 737 Max 8 with up to 180 passengers on board made an emergency landing at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport this morning after transmitting three emergency signals, one of which indicated what is known as a possible unlawful interference. Israeli media have reported dramatic testimonies and video from people on board, with some describing passengers storming the cockpit to subdue the attacker and one of the pilots being seriously injured.
The Israeli national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, said the incident highlighted the need for Israel to escalate its military campaigns across the region.

“Thank God and the heroic passengers, but Israel’s security doctrine must be taken to the next level,” he wrote on X, adding that the country “must continue until achieving total victory” in Iran, Lebanon, Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

“The naive notion that our enemies value life and deserve our pity was given yet another stark reminder this morning in the form of a terrorist who planned to blow up a plane and murder the 180 Israelis on board.”

Similarly, the Israeli finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, said that “anyone who tried to bring down a plane and murder 180 Israelis should pay as though they had murdered them – as should any country or terrorist organisation that sent them”.

According to the Israeli Hareetz newspaper, citing an unnamed official, authorities were treating it as a “terror” incident and “believe that one of the pilots may have purposefully attempted to crash the plane”. The newspaper added that other scenarios were also being considered.

Commenting this morning, the Israeli prime minister’s office said the situation was “under control” while measures are being taken to bring the passengers to Israel. Local media reported the military had scrambled fighter jets after fears of a possible hijacking, which the prime minister’s office had ruled out shortly after the incident came to light.
In a statement, Tabuk airport said the flight that was bound for Tel Aviv landed at 9.45am local time and that its captain and co-pilot “were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital”.
FlyDubai said flight FZ 1073 “experienced an incident while en route” and that all passengers “are safe and accounted for”.

articles.title: Europe ‘faces window of vulnerability until 2030,’ Dutch chief of defence warns - Europe live
articles.author: Martin Belam (now) and Jakub Krupa (earlier)

paras.en: Europe 'faces window of vulnerability until 2030,' Dutch chief of defence warns

The chief of defence of the Dutch armed forces, Gen Onno Eichelsheim, said that Europe urgently needs to learn from the lessons of Ukraine, as Europe is “facing a window of vulnerability until 2030” as it races to rearm itself.
Speaking at the Euronews Defence and Space Summit, he said there is “a gap between today’s threats and an armed force that will only be ready several years from now.”
“Within that window, we must ensure that strong deterrence is in place, and if deterrence fails, we have to fight,” he said.

Eichelsheim also spoke about the need to make the right decisions on procurement and industrial cooperation and work together, not in solely national interests, to move at pace required. “We don’t need 27 different drone programmes,” he said.
“The success of European defence cooperation will not be measured by the number of programmes we create, but by the equipment we put in the hands of our soldiers,” he said.
He said the EU’s tools “only work if we use them in the right way,” whereas the European defence matchmaking programmes at the moment are “like Tinder, with all the same frustrations.”

“To make a match, you need a sufficient number of participants on the platform and once a match is made, someone must take action. And it is clear that member states, my own included, are not putting all of our project projects on that platform.

Furthermore, the information provided is often not detailed enough to enable meaningful matches, just as on Tinder. Profiles do not always reflect all reality, and even when you do get a match, someone has to respond.”
At one point, fearing that he’s taking this analogy a bit too far, he rushed to assure the audience that he does not, actually, spend that much time on Tinder and is happily married.
But he continued with his serious point:

“Too often we still begin by asking what share of defence industry contracts can my own country secure? Only after we have established that we look at partners, and only then do we accept attempts to make defence cooperation work. So we must reverse that logic.”
The Romanian parliament has again failed to elect a prime minister, prolonging a political crisis that has been ongoing since a pro-European coalition government collapsed in May.

Liberal European parliament member Siegfried Muresan failed to get lawmakers’ backing with just 182 of the 233 votes needed to approve his government, according to the official count, AFP reports, bringing the prospect of snap elections closer. President Nicusor Dan has now nominated three candidates for the post of prime minister, but all have failed to successfully form a government.
The Council of Europe has said that Ukrainians have made nearly 200,000 claims for compensation over Russia’s invasion since 2022.
AFP reports the body said about 65,000 of the 195,000 damages claims made since its Ukraine register opened in 2024 in The Hague had been accepted and the rest were being reviewed.

The council said claims can now be made in 43 different categories ranging from loss of human life or injury, to deprivation of medical care and education and fallout on the environment and natural resources.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has posted to social media to say that he has visited frontline troops in Ukraine’s east. Accompanying a video clip, the Ukrainian leader said:

Today, I met here with the warriors carrying out missions in the Lyman sector and presented them with state awards. I also spoke with the brigade commander about the missions the unit is carrying out.
EU's Kubilius calls for 'peace through strength' and further support for Ukraine
European defence commissioner Andrius Kubilius called for a push to achieve “peace through strength” as Russia continues to be not interested in any diplomatic talks on Ukraine.
Speaking at the Euronews event, he warned there were clear signs that “Russia is escalating,” but there is no immediate sign of political decision to strike further.
“Russians have capability to do some big things - one drone, ten drones, hundred drones, flying into Lithuania. I would not be surprised if that were to happen.

But do they have a really clear political decision to do something? I don’t know, and for me all our discussions about [whether] the Russians will do something are based on some sort of theoretical predictions.”

He said Europe in any case “needs to be ready” as “winter could be very rough,” but more attention should be paid to Ukraine’s growing capabilities, including its ability to strike targets within Russia.
“Ukraine really is defending not only themselves, but they are defending the whole Europe. And we need to make that a real priority for us,” he said.
He said it was “difficult to predict” what Russia could do in the future, but any signs of being afraid of Russia would only “encourage Putin to be even more escalatory.”
“Our support [for] Ukraine should be very clear answer to whatever Putin is trying to escalate,” he said.
Ukraine struggling to cover funding gap as war costs surge with drones, missiles, PM says

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s total war costs will reach $155bn this year and the government is struggling to close a $27bn funding gap to ensure it can still conduct combat operations at the start of 2027,prime minister Sergii Koretskyi said.

Koretskyi said the government planned to cover $7bn of the gap by postponing expenditure, reallocating money from other parts of the budget and cutting some costs, and was in talks with partners on how to cover the remaining $20bn, Reuters reported.

It is the first time Kyiv has released an estimate of its annual war costs, meaning there is no comparable figure for 2025, but officials have said that the cost of the conflict has risen as the use of missile and drone technology has increased.
Russia's hybrid threats no longer 'an eastern flank problem' as they 'move closer to our red lines,' Lithuanian chief of defence says
Lithuanian chief of defence Raimundas Vaikšnoras issued a similar warning about Russia’s escalating actions in Europe.
“We often imagine that war begins with tanks crossing the border. We wait for a clear Article 5 scenario.

But Russia is already operating below [the threshold for] Article 5. In Lithuania, we see indirect these threats as drone attacks in our airspace, sabotage and arson, cyberattacks, GPS jamming, the use of illegal migration as a tool …

For years, it was seen as an eastern flank problem. Not any more. We see the same methods increasingly used across Europe. The purpose is clear to test our resiliency, find our weak points and challenge ally unity.
So the question is, if this is happening now, what is next?
Russia will continue to test how far it can go if there is no effective response. Each successful test creates space for the next one.
More pressure on critical infrastructure, energy network and our societies and attempt to slow down Nato decision making process before conventional conflict even begins.
Today, Russia operates below of Article 5. Tomorrow it may test how close it can get to that line.”
He warned that “we should not assume” that Russia will remain at the current threat level.
“It will test our limits. It will move closer to our red lines, and it may eventually test whether these lines can be erased.”
Vaikšnoras warned that meanwhile “all European procurement systems and legal frameworks still often work at peacetime speed.”
“If it takes years to test, buy and field new technologies, we risk buying yesterday’s technology for tomorrow’s wars,” he warned.
Europe 'faces window of vulnerability until 2030,' Dutch chief of defence warns

Furthermore, the information provided is often not detailed enough to enable meaningful matches, just as on Tinder. Profiles do not always reflect all reality, and even when you do get a match, someone has to respond.”
At one point, fearing that he’s taking this analogy a bit too far, he rushed to assure the audience that he does not, actually, spend that much time on Tinder and is happily married.
But he continued with his serious point:

“Too often we still begin by asking what share of defence industry contracts can my own country secure? Only after we have established that we look at partners, and only then do we accept attempts to make defence cooperation work. So we must reverse that logic.”
Five dead, 14 injured after overnight Russian strikes on Ukraine
Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine faced “a difficult attack” from Russia overnight with “nearly 190 attack drones, as well as ballistic missiles.”

“The main target was energy infrastructure in the capital and the Kyiv region. Residential buildings were also damaged. Work is ongoing to restore electricity and water supplies everywhere they are currently unavailable.”

“In the morning, a drone struck a grocery supermarket in Ivankovychi. First responders are extinguishing the fire. Kyiv is also under drone attack. A warehouse building was hit, and one person was killed. There were strikes on critical infrastructure in the Zhytomyr, Mykolaiv, Kirovohrad, and Rivne regions. There was also damage in the Odesa, Sumy, Kharkiv, Kherson, and Cherkasy regions.
As of now, fourteen people have been injured across the country as a result of all these strikes. Tragically, five people have been killed, including a child.”
Russia issues rare warning to Nato over Kaliningrad
Russia has warned Nato it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the alliance attempted to cut off Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave that borders the Baltic Sea, Reuters reported.

In a document sent to Nato, seen by Reuters, and first reported by Lithuanian media, Moscow accused the alliance of a “dangerous and reckless course” that entailed “high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict”.
The document said this included the possibility “of Russian strikes against decision-making centres in the alliance’s member states right from the outset of the conflict”.

“Russia will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory should Nato countries undertake any attempt aimed at isolating the Kaliningrad Region from the rest of the country,” said the text, classed as a “non-paper” — diplomatic jargon for an informal document.
Nato spokesperson Allison Hart confirmed Russia had sent a non-paper to the alliance but did not disclose its contents.

“We have sent a response, noting that Nato is a defensive Alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia. We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric. We call on Russia to end its unprovoked war in Ukraine,” she said.

Lithuania dismissed the Russian warning “completely baseless and seen as a measure of psychological pressure,”Deividas Matulionis, national security aide to president Gitanas Nausėda, told local media, as reported by LRT.
Brexit 'the biggest lie of the last 30 years,' Macron says

Meanwhile, with Brexit and the question of Britain’s relationship with the EU back in the spotlight in the UK, it’s worth picking up some fresh comments from France’s Emmanuel Macron, who is now on a state visit in Spain.
Speaking with students at the Universidad Complutense de Madrid last night, Macron took aim at Brexit calling it “the biggest lie of the last 30 years.”

In a long defence of Europe’s unique integration process – where, according to Macron, even nationalist leaders have come to appreciate the bloc’s role – he described Brexit as a “disastrous exception” to the rule.
“Brexit is the biggest lie of the last 30 years.

Those who said, ‘We’ll be richer,’ eight points of GDP less 10 years on. We’ll solve the immigration problem; it’s more complicated than before. And we’re going to be a huge success in international trade, it’s even worse.”
We will hear from him again later today, as he is expected to take part in a press conference with Spain’s Pedro Sánchez early afternoon.
Russia moves towards mass attacks on energy infrastructure, Ukraine's PM says

Russia has moved to mass attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure,Ukrainian prime minister Sergii Koretskyi said, after overnight strikes on energy facilities in the capital and other regions, Reuters reported.
“This was the first time such a massive and combined attack had taken place since the end of the last heating season,” Koretskyi said on Telegram.
'It will be a dark winter for Europe,' Belgium's defence minister warns
Belgian defence minister Theo Francken said “there will be more hybrid threat actions” in the coming months, as he starkly warned “it will be a dark winter for Europe.”

Speaking at Euronews’s Defence and Space Summit, Francken said hybrid warfare “is not something that Russia [has been] doing for two or three years,” but for much longer and it has “expertise” in this area, often making it difficult for western countries to investigate them and attribute responsibility.
He particularly worried about Russia’s increased use of jet-powered drones.
“We need to scale up our air defences and we need to have more stocks, scale up production. Everything has to go faster,” he said.
He said Belgium used to be “the worse pupil in class” two years ago with low defence spending, but it has since improved and ramped it up its planning.
He said Europe got too used to its comfortable welfare state protections at the cost of adequate spending on defence, and this is now changing.

“Europe has been very good in investing in soft power, in social security. And it’s beautiful to have a pension system, to have social welfare systems [for] when somebody gets sick, when somebody lost his job – we have everything. But when there’s war or there’s hybrid threats, we don’t have anything. So yeah, we’re in a really difficult position.”
Morning opening: Russia targets communications, energy facilities in Ukraine
Debris had been found at the premises of one of the western embassies in the centre of Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said this morning, citing preliminary information.
Klitschko did not name the embassy, but said emergency services were heading to the site.
It comes after another night of Russian drone attacks on Ukraine, which damaged energy facilities and other civilian infrastructure.
Russia said it targeted a communications centre and energy facilities in Kyiv, and port infrastructure in Izmail, among others.
In other news, Romanian parliament will vote on a third nominee for prime minister, with EU lawmaker Siegfried Mureșan expected to struggle to secure the required majority.

And France’s Emmanuel Macron continues his visit to Spain amid ongoing housing protests in the country. He is due to appear at a press conference with Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez later today.
It’s Wednesday, 30 September 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

articles.title: UK-France ‘one in one out’ deal to expire on Thursday, say sources
articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor

paras.en: The UK government’s “one in one out” deal with France, which was supposed to help deter small boat arrivals, is expected to expire on Thursday, government sources have said.
paras.zh: 政府消息人士称，英国政府与法国的“一对一”协议预计将于周四到期，该协议本应有助于阻止小船抵达。

paras.en: Negotiations to extend the deal have stalled over French demands for a Europe-wide deal instead, and a reluctance to scale up the numbers of people exchanged between the two countries.
Flights that remove people who have been already detained under the scheme will continue, but they are expected to end within weeks.
A UK government source confirmed that the expectation was that the deal would be formally drawn to a close on Thursday.

“We would like to see the deal continue. But it’s not the end of the world if it doesn’t because it never got to the scale where it would have been a proper deterrent to people coming to the UK in small boats,” the source said.
The French interior ministry told French media on Wednesday: “We are discussing with the British the terms of exiting the agreement.”
Negotiations in Paris over how best to tie up the deal are continuing between Home Office staff and their French counterparts.

More than 1,400 people who have arrived in the UK via small boats have been sent back to France under the deal. As of the end of June 2026, 1,117 people with links to the UK had been sent to the UK from France.
The deal had been set to expire in April but was extended to 1 October to help counter the anticipated increase in attempted crossings during the summer.
The scheme was announced by Keir Starmer and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in July 2025 and the first flights took off in September that year.
At the time, Starmer described the deal as “groundbreaking” because it would help to deter the number of people crossing the Channel illegally.
“There is no silver bullet here, but with a united effort, new tactics and a new level of intent, we can finally turn the tables,” he said.
Many of the detainees deported to France under the deal have become homeless in the French capital.
Others have returned to the camps around Calais and Dunkirk, and some have made the Channel crossing back to the UK.
In June, France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, lauded the scheme as a potential deterrent but said France was not prepared to go it alone with Britain.

“According to information from the UN high commissioner for refugees, word of the scheme is beginning to spread, which is prompting a number of migrants to abandon their plans to make the crossing,” Nuñez told a parliamentary commission.

“The value of this scheme is therefore clear. Nevertheless, we consider that France should not bear the burden alone and that it would be better to incorporate it into an agreement between the EU and the UK.
“I have therefore already made it clear to my counterpart that this pilot agreement, which we signed in August 2025, was not intended to be extended beyond 1 October 2026.”
An EU-wide returns deal known as the Dublin agreement existed before the UK left the EU. Attempts to continue the returns deal post-Brexit have been rejected by EU leaders.
Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, disclosed to MPs this month that the deal cost about £56,000 for every person sent back to France.

She dismissed suggestions that an EU-wide system would be a “silver bullet” for the Channel crisis. She said: “It is a real mistake to think that that pact is the future. And if we were in that, this problem would go away, because I promise you it would not.”

She added that the government’s scheme had struggled to scale up to larger numbers of returns and it had been “operationally difficult” to increase removals because of constraints such as detention space.
“It’s not been without its challenges. Obviously, the numbers are still relatively small,” she said.
Between January and 27 September, 19,135 people crossed the Channel by small boat from France. This was down by 42% on the same period the previous year.

articles.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends

paras.en: The last British and American troops have left Iraq after a military presence of more than a decade in the country.
paras.zh: 最后一批英国和美国军队在伊拉克驻军十多年后离开了伊拉克。

paras.en: The exit of the remaining UK military personnel - around 100 - from Irbil, in the northern Kurdistan region, was co-ordinated over recent weeks with US forces, who also departed on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 其余约100名英国军事人员从库尔德斯坦北部地区的埃尔比勒撤离，最近几周与美军进行了协调，美军也于周三撤离。

paras.en: It follows an agreement between the US and the Iraqi government, signed two years ago, to withdraw foreign troops by the end of this month.
paras.zh: 两年前，美国和伊拉克政府签署了一项协议，在本月底之前撤出外国军队。

paras.en: British and US forces have been present in Iraq since 2014, as part of the international coalition to help defeat the extremist Islamic State (IS) group. Their departure brings the mission, known as Operation Inherent Resolve, to an end.
paras.zh: 自2014年以来，英国和美国军队一直驻扎在伊拉克，作为帮助击败极端主义伊斯兰国（ IS ）组织的国际联盟的一部分。他们的离开结束了被称为固有决心行动（ Operation Inherent Resolve ）的任务。

paras.en: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said the end of the coalition's mission marked "Iraq's transition to a phase in which it assumes full responsibility for its security and stability".
paras.zh: 伊拉克总理阿里·扎伊迪（ Ali al-Zaidi ）表示，联盟任务的结束标志着“伊拉克过渡到对其安全和稳定承担全部责任的阶段”。

paras.en: Iraq is set to hold four "Sovereignty Days" as a national holiday to mark the withdrawal.
paras.zh: 伊拉克将举行四个“主权日”作为国定假日，以纪念撤军。

paras.en: "Following more than a decade of operations, training and capacity building, Iraqi Security Forces (ISF) and the Kurdish Peshmerga have secured the enduring territorial defeat of Daesh in Iraq and are now well placed to take primary responsibility for the country's security," the UK Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement, referring to IS by an Arabic acronym.
paras.zh: 英国国防部在一份声明中表示： “经过十多年的行动、培训和能力建设，伊拉克安全部队（ ISF ）和库尔德Peshmerga已确保ISIS在伊拉克的持久领土失败，现在完全有能力承担对该国安全的主要责任。”

paras.en: "With these objectives achieved, Iraq and its international partners can begin a new chapter focused on enduring security co-operation under Iraqi leadership."
paras.zh: “随着这些目标的实现，伊拉克及其国际伙伴可以开启新的篇章，重点关注伊拉克领导下的持久安全合作。”

paras.en: Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the coalition's departure from Irbil marked "the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated [IS] in Iraq".
paras.zh: 五角大楼发言人肖恩·帕内尔（ Sean Parnell ）表示，该联盟离开埃尔比勒标志着“在伊拉克击败[伊斯兰国]的军事任务圆满结束”。

paras.en: He added: "The primary responsibility for addressing Iraq's remaining security challenges, including [IS] remnants and Iran-aligned militias that undermine Iraqi sovereignty and regional stability, now rests with the government of Iraq."
paras.zh: 他补充说： “解决伊拉克剩余安全挑战的主要责任，包括破坏伊拉克主权和地区稳定的[IS]残余分子和与伊朗结盟的民兵，现在由伊拉克政府承担。”

paras.en: The Iraqi government declared the military defeat of IS in 2017, but coalition forces remained to help prevent the group's resurgence.
paras.zh: 伊拉克政府于2017年宣布在军事上击败伊斯兰国，但联军仍在帮助防止该组织的复苏。

paras.en: A recent UN report estimated that sustained counter-terrorism pressure by Iraqi security forces had left IS with several hundred fighters who were "able to carry out unsophisticated operations only".
paras.zh: 联合国最近的一份报告估计，伊拉克安全部队持续的反恐压力使伊斯兰国拥有数百名战斗人员，他们“只能执行不复杂的行动”。

paras.en: The Iraqi government also faces the challenge of Iranian-backed militias in the country.
paras.zh: 伊拉克政府还面临伊朗支持的民兵的挑战。

paras.en: Zaidi, who took office in May, has vowed to disarm them and bring all weapons under state control following the coalition's exit.
paras.zh: 扎伊迪于5月上任，他发誓要在联盟退出后解除他们的武装，并将所有武器置于国家控制之下。

paras.en: But several powerful factions have resisted his plans and could now see their influence grow without the US presence.
paras.zh: 但一些强大的派系抵制了他的计划，现在可以在没有美国存在的情况下看到他们的影响力增长。

paras.en: Since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran earlier this year, militias have been targeting the remaining US and UK forces stationed at Irbil air base.
paras.zh: 自今年早些时候美国和以色列与伊朗的战争开始以来，民兵一直在瞄准驻扎在埃尔比勒空军基地的剩余美英部队。

paras.en: Hundreds of Nato troops stationed in Baghdad left the country in March as tensions rose.
paras.zh: 随着紧张局势加剧，驻扎在巴格达的数百名北约部队于3月离开该国。

paras.en: A BBC team visited the coalition base in Irbil in April this year, during a fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran.
paras.zh: 今年4月，在美国和伊朗之间脆弱的停火期间，英国广播公司的一个团队访问了埃尔比勒的联军基地。

paras.en: They were forced to circle the base in an RAF transport aircraft while drones were being launched nearby.
paras.zh: 当无人机在附近发射时，他们被迫乘坐英国皇家空军运输机在基地上空盘旋。

paras.en: At the height of the US bombing campaign against Iran, the coalition base was being targeted by up to 28 drones and missiles a day.
paras.zh: 在美国轰炸伊朗的高峰期，联军基地每天多达28架无人机和导弹袭击目标。

paras.en: RAF Regiment Gunners, who were among the last British military personnel stationed there, had shot down more than 100 drones in the first six weeks of the war. Many of the attack drones were being launched by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq.
paras.zh: 英国皇家空军炮兵团是驻扎在那里的最后一批英国军事人员之一，他们在战争的前六周击落了100多架无人机。许多攻击无人机是由伊朗支持的伊拉克民兵发射的。

paras.en: On Wednesday, signalling the end of the mission, the MoD paid tribute to UK personnel who had contributed to the counter-IS mission.
paras.zh: 周三，标志着任务的结束，国防部向为打击伊斯兰国任务做出贡献的英国人员表示敬意。

paras.en: It said they had provided "valuable support, training and assistance" to more than 111,000 members of the Iraqi Security Forces, including more than 21,000 Peshmerga forces in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan Region.
paras.zh: 它说，他们向伊拉克安全部队的111,000多名成员提供了“宝贵的支持，培训和援助” ，其中包括半自治库尔德斯坦地区的21,000多名佩什梅加部队。

paras.en: It also said the RAF had conducted thousands of sorties, striking more than 2,300 IS targets. The RAF is expected to continue flying missions over neighbouring Syria, to prevent the remnants of IS from gaining a foothold.
paras.zh: 它还说，英国皇家空军出动了数千架次，打击了2300多个IS目标。预计英国皇家空军将继续在邻国叙利亚上空执行飞行任务，以防止伊斯兰国的残余势力获得立足点。

paras.en: The Pentagon said the US would continue to provide "targeted training and intelligence support" to its Iraqi partners.
paras.zh: 五角大楼表示，美国将继续向伊拉克合作伙伴提供“有针对性的培训和情报支持”。

paras.en: US Central Command said the coalition's joint taskforce remained operational and was now based in Jordan.
paras.zh: 美国中央司令部表示，该联盟的联合特遣部队仍在运作，目前驻扎在约旦。

paras.en: US forces will also continue their mission against IS in Syria, where the UN estimates that the group has up to 3,000 fighters.
paras.zh: 美军还将继续在叙利亚执行打击伊斯兰国的任务，联合国估计该组织在叙利亚拥有多达3000名战斗人员。

paras.en: This is the third time US and UK forces have withdrawn from Iraq.
paras.zh: 这是美英部队第三次从伊拉克撤军。

paras.en: Tens of thousands of US and British troops were deployed to the country in 1991 following Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait.
paras.zh: 1991年，在萨达姆入侵科威特之后，成千上万的美国和英国军队被部署到该国。

paras.en: They returned to Iraq in 2003, when US President George W Bush ordered Operation Iraqi Freedom to remove the dictator from power and eliminate weapons of mass destruction that turned out not to exist.
paras.zh: 他们于2003年返回伊拉克，当时美国总统乔治· W ·布什命令伊拉克自由行动将独裁者赶下台，并消除原本不存在的大规模毁灭性武器。

paras.en: The fierce sectarian insurgency that engulfed Iraq following the invasion cost tens of thousands of lives, including those of nearly 4,500 US military personnel and 179 British military personnel.
paras.zh: 入侵后席卷伊拉克的激烈宗派叛乱造成数万人死亡，其中包括近4500名美国军事人员和179名英国军事人员。

paras.en: US and UK forces left Iraq in 2011, only to return three years later, when IS threatened to take control of the country.
paras.zh: 美国和英国军队于2011年离开伊拉克，三年后才返回，当时伊斯兰国威胁要控制该国。

articles.title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering elephants for independence celebrations

paras.en: Animal rights activists have criticised Botswana's decision to authorise the killing of 23 elephants to provide meat for independence celebrations.
paras.zh: 动物权利活动人士批评博茨瓦纳决定授权杀死23头大象，为独立庆祝活动提供肉类。

paras.en: The southern African country, home to the world's largest elephant population, is holding nationwide festivities on Wednesday to mark the 60th anniversary of independence from Britain.
paras.zh: 这个拥有世界上最大象群的南部非洲国家将于周三举行全国性的庆祝活动，以纪念脱离英国独立60周年。

paras.en: A licence issued by the Ministry of Environment and Tourism, seen by local media, authorises the hunting of 23 elephants and other wild animals for "complimentary purposes".
paras.zh: 当地媒体看到环境和旅游部颁发的许可证，授权出于“免费目的”狩猎23头大象和其他野生动物。

paras.en: The Botswana-based Elephant Protection Society warns the decision could undermine conservation, with its chairman Oaitse Nawa telling the BBC elephants needed greater protection.
paras.zh: 总部位于博茨瓦纳的大象保护协会警告说，这一决定可能会破坏保护工作，其主席Oaitse Nawa告诉BBC大象需要更多的保护。

paras.en: He warned that slaughtering elephants for celebratory feasting could encourage poaching by creating the impression that killing elephants is acceptable when sanctioned by government.
paras.zh: 他警告说，为庆祝盛宴而屠宰大象可能会给人留下一种印象，即在政府批准的情况下杀死大象是可以接受的，从而鼓励偷猎。

paras.en: "Elephants have lost their social structures because they are always being pushed from one place to another by gunshots," Nawa said.
paras.zh: Nawa说： “大象已经失去了它们的社会结构，因为它们总是被枪声从一个地方推到另一个地方。”

paras.en: Several social media users in the country have also expressed concerns about eating the game meat amid an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, which has prompted authorities to impose measures to contain its spread.
paras.zh: 该国的一些社交媒体用户也对在口蹄疫爆发期间食用游戏肉类表示担忧，这促使当局采取措施遏制其传播。

paras.en: Tshenatshe Monwela, an elder in Maun, a tourism town in north-western Botswana told local media that his community should have received buffalo instead.
paras.zh: 博茨瓦纳西北部旅游小镇Maun的长老Tshenatshe Monwela告诉当地媒体，他的社区应该得到水牛。

paras.en: He argued that elephants had particular cultural and ecological significance and that Botswana's historic role in protecting the country's wildlife and livestock should have been recognised in the government's allocation of meat for the anniversary celebrations.
paras.zh: 他认为，大象具有特殊的文化和生态意义，博茨瓦纳在保护国家野生动植物和牲畜方面的历史性作用应该在政府为周年庆祝活动分配肉类时得到承认。

paras.en: Botswana's government has organised a series of events to mark the country's diamond jubilee, including a carnival in the capital, Gaborone, as well as cultural performances, concerts and sporting events.
paras.zh: 博茨瓦纳政府已组织了一系列活动来纪念该国的钻石禧年，包括在首都哈博罗内的狂欢节，以及文化表演、音乐会和体育赛事。

paras.en: The game meat is expected to be served as part of the traditional feasting associated with the Independence Day celebrations.
paras.zh: 游戏肉预计将作为与独立日庆祝活动相关的传统盛宴的一部分。

paras.en: The 23 elephants were allocated in eight districts across the country.
paras.zh: 这23头大象分布在全国8个地区。

paras.en: It was not immediately clear how many of the animals had been killed by Wednesday morning. The BBC has asked the government for comment.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚到周三早上有多少动物被杀。英国广播公司已要求政府置评。

paras.en: But local media published images from different parts of Botswana showing residents gathering around elephant carcasses, some with knives in hand and sharing the meat.
paras.zh: 但当地媒体发布了博茨瓦纳不同地区的图像，显示居民聚集在大象尸体周围，其中一些人手持刀具并分享肉类。

paras.en: In Chobe, a wildlife-rich district in northern Botswana near the borders with Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe, a local MP raised concerns after residents reportedly collected portions directly from a carcass at a school.
paras.zh: 在博茨瓦纳北部靠近纳米比亚、赞比亚和津巴布韦边界的一个野生动物丰富的地区乔贝（ Chobe ） ，一名当地议员提出了担忧，据报道，当地居民直接从一所学校的尸体上收集了一部分。

paras.en: He said the system risked creating congestion and disadvantaging elderly people, pregnant women and people with disabilities, and suggested the meat should instead be processed into 5kg or 10kg packages to improve hygiene and ensure fairer distribution.
paras.zh: 他说，该系统有可能造成拥堵，使老年人、孕妇和残疾人处于不利地位，并建议将肉类加工成5公斤或10公斤的包装，以改善卫生并确保更公平的分配。

paras.en: "For the sake of dignity, fairness and public hygiene, we respectfully call on the hunter and the relevant leadership to ensure that future distributions are properly organised," MP Simasiku Mapulanga posted on Facebook, attaching photos of people scrambling for meat around an elephant carcass.
paras.zh: “为了尊严、公平和公共卫生，我们恭敬地呼吁猎人和相关领导层确保未来的分配得到妥善组织，”议员Simasiku Mapulanga在Facebook上发布，附上人们在大象尸体周围争抢肉类的照片。

paras.en: Elephant meat is common in some wildlife-rich communities, particularly when meat from legal hunts is distributed locally, but it is not an everyday staple.
paras.zh: 大象肉在一些野生动物丰富的社区很常见，特别是当合法狩猎的肉类在当地分销时，但它并不是日常生活的主食。

paras.en: Botswana also tightly regulates game meat, and its legal possession generally depends on proving it came from a lawful hunt.
paras.zh: 博茨瓦纳还严格监管野味肉类，其合法占有通常取决于证明其来自合法狩猎。

paras.en: The decision has reignited a long-running and often heated debate in Botswana over how the country manages its huge elephant population.
paras.zh: 这一决定在博茨瓦纳重新引发了一场长期且经常激烈的辩论，讨论该国如何管理其庞大的大象种群。

paras.en: Botswana has more than 130,000 elephants and communities living alongside them have long complained about animals destroying crops, damaging property and sometimes killing people.
paras.zh: 博茨瓦纳有超过13万头大象，与它们生活在一起的社区长期以来一直抱怨动物破坏庄稼、破坏财产，有时还会杀人。

paras.en: The government has defended regulated hunting as one way of managing the elephant population and human-wildlife conflict while generating income for communities.
paras.zh: 政府为受监管的狩猎辩护，将其作为管理大象种群和人类与野生动物冲突的一种方式，同时为社区创造收入。

paras.en: The country banned trophy hunting in 2014 under former President Ian Khama but lifted the restrictions five years later under his successor, Mokgweetsi Masisi.
paras.zh: 在前总统伊恩·卡马（ Ian Khama ）的领导下，该国于2014年禁止狩猎奖杯，但五年后在他的继任者莫克韦齐·马西西（ Mokgweetsi Masisi ）的领导下取消了限制

paras.en: Hunting has continued under President Duma Boko, who defeated Masisi in elections in 2024.
paras.zh: 在杜马·博科总统的领导下，狩猎仍在继续，他在2024年的选举中击败了马西西。

paras.en: The government says proceeds from hunting supports conservation and local development.
paras.zh: 政府表示，狩猎收入支持保护和当地发展。

paras.en: Minister of Environment and Tourism Wynter Mmolotsi told parliament last year that special elephant quotas raised 15.6m pula ($1.1m; Â£820,000) in 2025 for projects in areas where elephants are found.
paras.zh: 环境和旅游部长Wynter Mmolotsi去年告诉议会， 2025年，为发现大象的地区的项目筹集了1560万普拉（ 110万美元； 82万英镑）的特殊大象配额。

paras.en: But conservation organisations have questioned whether the level of hunting is sustainable.
paras.zh: 但保护组织质疑狩猎水平是否可持续。

paras.en: Supporters of Botswana's hunting policy, however, argue that international criticism often overlooks the costs borne by rural communities living alongside one of the world's biggest concentrations of elephants.
paras.zh: 然而，博茨瓦纳狩猎政策的支持者认为，国际批评往往忽视了生活在世界上最大的大象集中地之一的农村社区所承担的成本。

paras.en: They say elephants destroy crops and infrastructure and pose a danger to people, particularly as their range increasingly overlaps with farms and settlements.
paras.zh: 他们说，大象摧毁了庄稼和基础设施，对人类构成了危险，特别是因为它们的种植范围越来越多地与农场和定居点重叠。

articles.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring

paras.en: Russia has launched the largest attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the spring, primarily targeting Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi has said.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总理谢尔希·科列茨基（ Serhiy Koretskyi ）表示，自今年春天以来，俄罗斯对乌克兰的能源基础设施发动了规模最大的袭击，主要针对基辅及其周边地区。

paras.en: At least five people were killed in overnight attacks across the country, including a child in the Kyiv region, Koretskyi said.
paras.zh: 科列茨基说，全国至少有5人在连夜袭击中丧生，其中包括基辅地区的一名儿童。

paras.en: The strikes also impacted people's power supplies, with Ukraine's biggest private energy firm, DTEK, saying power to 8,000 homes had been restored following "a difficult night" for the capital.
paras.zh: 罢工还影响了人们的电力供应，乌克兰最大的私营能源公司DTEK表示，在首都“艰难的夜晚”之后， 8000户家庭的电力已经恢复。

paras.en: The Russian defence ministry said one of its targets was the Trypilska power station, the largest supplier of electricity to Kyiv.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯国防部表示，其目标之一是基辅最大的电力供应商Trypilska发电站。

paras.en: In a statement on Telegram, Koretskyi said: "Since the summer, there has effectively not been a single day without enemy attacks on our energy infrastructure.
paras.zh: 在Telegram上的一份声明中， Koretskyi说： “自夏季以来，实际上没有一天没有敌人攻击我们的能源基础设施。

paras.en: "However, a mass and combined attack of this scale has occurred for the first time since the end of the last heating season."
paras.zh: “然而，自上个供暖季节结束以来，这种规模的大规模联合攻击首次发生。”

paras.en: Ukraine has been expecting another protracted Russian assault on the country's energy grid. It has happened every winter so far since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
paras.zh: 乌克兰一直期待俄罗斯对该国能源网发动另一次旷日持久的攻击。自2022年俄罗斯全面入侵以来，每年冬天都会发生这种情况。

paras.en: In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings, social infrastructure, civilian enterprises and railways also targeted, Koretskyi said.
paras.zh: Koretskyi说，该国共有11个地区在一夜之间遭到袭击，住宅楼，社会基础设施，民用企业和铁路也成为袭击目标。

paras.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said there were strikes on critical infrastructure in the Zhytomyr, Mykolaiv, Kirovohrad and Rivne regions.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelensky ）表示，日托米尔（ Zhytomyr ）、尼古拉耶夫（ Mykolaiv ）、基洛沃格勒（ Kirovohrad ）和里夫内（ Rivne ）地区的关键基础设

paras.en: On Wednesday, some households in the Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Sumy, Kyiv and Kharkiv regions remained without power, Ukraine's energy ministry said.
paras.zh: 乌克兰能源部表示，周三，基辅、第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克、顿涅茨克、苏梅、基辅和哈尔科夫地区的一些家庭仍然没有电力供应。

paras.en: State-owned grid operator Ukrenegro advised residents not to use powerful electrical appliances between the hours of 10:00 and 16:00 local time as electricity supplies were lower than usual.
paras.zh: 国有电网运营商Ukrenegro建议居民在当地时间10:00至16:00之间不要使用强大的电器，因为电力供应低于平时。

paras.en: Russia's defence ministry said it had launched massive overnight strikes on Ukrainian facilities.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯国防部表示，它已对乌克兰设施发动了大规模的夜间罢工。

paras.en: It said its targets included the Trypilska thermal power plant, located some 40km from Kyiv, and claimed the plant supplied electricity to Ukrainian defence facilities.
paras.zh: 它表示，其目标包括距离基辅约40公里的Trypilska热电厂，并声称该电厂向乌克兰国防设施供电。

paras.en: The operator of the plant, Centrenergo, confirmed that the plant had been damaged in a Russian attack and that it was assessing the scale of the damage.
paras.zh: 该工厂的运营商Centrenergo证实，该工厂在俄罗斯的袭击中受损，并且正在评估损坏的规模。

paras.en: In Kyiv, people woke to find the city blanketed by thick, acrid smoke after a night punctuated by the sound of explosions. An air raid alert was still on and the distant sound of air defence gunfire echoed through the murky atmosphere.
paras.zh: 在基辅，人们醒来时发现这座城市被浓烈刺鼻的烟雾笼罩，晚上被爆炸声打断。空袭警报仍在，远处的防空炮声在朦胧的气氛中回荡。

paras.en: Residents in several districts were advised to close their windows until the smoke cleared.
paras.zh: 几个地区的居民被建议关闭窗户，直到烟雾消散。

paras.en: Among those killed in the overnight strikes was a child whose body was found under the rubble of a house, Kyiv regional governor Timur Tkachenko said.
paras.zh: 基辅地区总督蒂穆尔·特卡琴科（ Timur Tkachenko ）说，在夜间罢工中丧生的人中，有一名儿童的尸体被发现在一所房屋的废墟下。

paras.en: Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klischko said three people were killed in total in the capital, including a Ukrainian utility company worker who was killed at a warehouse building.
paras.zh: 基辅市长维塔利·克里希科（ Vitaly Klischko ）表示，首都共有3人遇难，其中包括一名在仓库大楼遇害的乌克兰公用事业公司工人。

paras.en: Another person was killed in the Mykolaiv region, acting regional governor Heorhiy Reshetilov said.
paras.zh: 代理地区州长Heorhiy Reshetilov说，另一人在尼古拉耶夫地区被杀。

paras.en: Two more people were also killed in the north-eastern Sumy region on Tuesday, governor Oleh Hryhorov said. A school was also hit there in a separate strike, he added.
paras.zh: 州长奥莱赫·赫里霍罗夫（ Oleh Hryhorov ）说，周二在苏梅岛东北部地区还有两人遇难。他补充说，一所学校也在另一次罢工中被击中。

paras.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（ Vladimir Putin ）于2022年发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵，莫斯科目前控制着乌克兰约20 ％的领土。
